title: Huawei Found Guilty in Brooklyn: The 8-Year Case, the Arrested CFO and the Charge That Failed
description:
On November 24, 2026, a federal jury in Brooklyn convicted Huawei on 10 of 12 counts, including bank fraud, Iran sanctions violations and conspiracy to steal trade secrets, but cleared it of racketeering. Here is the full story, from Meng Wanzhou's 2018 arrest in Vancouver to the verdict.
Proven: the jury convicted Huawei on 10 of 12 counts and acquitted it of racketeering conspiracy and conspiracy to obstruct justice; Meng Wanzhou signed a statement of facts in 2021 that the judge allowed at trial; sentencing is set for September 2027.
Debated: whether the verdict survives an appeal (Huawei says it fully expects to appeal and calls the charges without merit), how large the penalty will be, and whether the case is about crime or the US-China technology race.
Sources: US Justice Department statements, Fortune, Bloomberg, Reuters (via Al Jazeera), AP (via Broadband Breakfast), The Next Web, South China Morning Post.
Animated with code, narration is synthetic. Facts as of Nov 26, 2026.
